One decoder-only causal transformer block containing masked self-attention and an internal Dense/FC feed-forward path.

Connect Float32 [batch, sequence, d_model]. Internal Q/K/V/output projections and the feed-forward path (Dense -> activation -> Dense, or a gated GLU-family FFN) are owned by this composite node. Change dim_feedforward for its hidden width; stack TransformerDecoder nodes to add depth. Connected Memory remains fail-closed until seq2seq cross-attention has a graph owner.

## Settings

| Group | Setting | Key | Type | Default | Allowed values | Read by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Transformer | Model Width | `d_model` | Integer | `512` | `1-65536` | The run | Required input/output feature width. Required. |
| Transformer | Attention Heads | `num_heads` | Integer | `8` | `1-4096` | The run | Attention heads; d_model must divide evenly. Required. |
| Transformer | Feed-forward Width | `dim_feedforward` | Integer | `2048` | `1-1048576` | The run | Inner feed-forward feature width. Required. |
| Regularization | Dropout | `dropout` | Number | `0.0` | `0.0-0.999` | The run | Training dropout probability. Keep zero for strict ArrayFire causal-LM training; nonzero dropout remains a compatibility path until transformer-dropout residency is proven for this graph contract. |
| Regularization | FFN Hidden Dropout | `ffn_dropout` | Number | `0.0` | `0.0-0.999` | The run | Dropout after FFN activation, before its second Dense; zero preserves legacy blocks. |
| Transformer | Pre-Norm | `norm_first` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Apply normalization before each sublayer (pre-norm, as in GPT-2 and LLaMA). Off is the original post-norm layout. Advanced. |
| Block | Architecture Preset | `architecture_preset` | Choice | `custom` | `custom`, `classic`, `gpt2_style`, `llama_style` | The run | Fill the block fields for a known design. classic: the 2017 block (post-norm LayerNorm, ReLU MLP, biases, external positions). gpt2_style: pre-norm LayerNorm, GELU MLP, biases, external positions (use a Positional Encoding node with encoding_type=learned). llama_style: pre-norm RMSNorm, SwiGLU feed-forward, RoPE, no biases. Widths, heads, dropout, epsilon and RoPE base stay yours (LLaMA sizes the gated feed-forward at about 8/3 x d_model to keep the parameter count). Editing any block field afterwards switches this to custom. |
| Block | Normalization | `norm_type` | Choice | `layer_norm` | `layer_norm`, `rms_norm` | The run | Normalization: layer_norm (mean and variance, learned scale and shift) or rms_norm (root-mean-square scale only, as in LLaMA; cheaper). |
| Block | Norm Epsilon | `norm_eps` | Number | `0.00001` | `0.0-1.0` | The run | Epsilon added inside the normalization square root. Advanced. |
| Block | Feed-forward Type | `ffn_type` | Choice | `mlp` | `mlp`, `gated` | The run | Feed-forward type: mlp = Dense -> activation -> Dense; gated = Dense(gate) -> activation, multiplied by Dense(up), then Dense(down). Gated with silu is SwiGLU (LLaMA), with gelu GEGLU, with relu ReGLU, with sigmoid GLU. Gated adds a third d_model x dim_feedforward matrix. |
| Block | Feed-forward Activation | `ffn_activation` | Choice | `relu` | `relu`, `gelu`, `gelu_exact`, `silu`, `mish`, `elu`, `selu`, `leaky_relu`, `sigmoid`, `tanh`, `hardswish`, `squared_relu` | The run | Feed-forward activation (the gate activation when ffn_type=gated). gelu is the tanh approximation (GPT-2), gelu_exact the erf form (BERT, PyTorch default); silu is Swish; squared_relu is relu(x)^2 (Primer). |
| Block | Feed-forward Bias | `ffn_bias` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Learn bias vectors in the feed-forward Dense layers. LLaMA-style blocks turn this off. Advanced. |
| Block | Position Encoding | `position_encoding` | Choice | `external` | `external`, `rope`, `alibi` | The run | Where positions come from: external (a Positional Encoding node before the blocks), rope (rotary position embedding inside self-attention, as in LLaMA; needs an even head width) or alibi (a per-head linear distance penalty on the attention scores, Press et al. 2022; handles texts longer than the training context). With rope or alibi, remove the Positional Encoding node. |
| Block | RoPE Base | `rope_base` | Number | `10000` | `1.0-10000000.0` | The run | Rotary frequency base (theta). Larger values suit longer contexts. Advanced. |
| Block | Attention Bias | `attention_bias` | On / off | `true` |   | The run | Learn bias vectors in the attention query, key, value and output projections. LLaMA-style blocks turn this off. |
| Block | QK Norm | `qk_norm` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | QK-norm: RMS-normalize each head's queries and keys (learned scale per head feature, shared across heads) before the attention scores, as in OLMo 2, Gemma 3 and Qwen3. Keeps attention logits bounded, which allows higher learning rates. Uses Norm Epsilon. |
| Block | RoPE Fraction | `rope_fraction` | Number | `1.0` | `0.01-1.0` | The run | Partial RoPE: fraction of each head's features that are rotated (GPT-NeoX 0.25, Phi 0.5); the rest carry no position signal. 1 rotates all. RoPE only. Advanced. |
| Block | Block Layout | `block_layout` | Choice | `sequential` | `sequential`, `parallel` | The run | sequential: attention then feed-forward, each with its own residual. parallel (GPT-J, PaLM): attention and feed-forward both read the same normalized input and are added together, x + attn(n(x)) + ffn(n(x)); faster per step. Parallel needs Pre-Norm. |
| Block | Sandwich Norm | `sandwich_norm` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Sandwich norm (Gemma 2/3): also normalize each sub-layer's output before the residual add, x + norm(attn(norm(x))). Stabilises deep or high-learning-rate training. Needs Pre-Norm; not with parallel layout. |
| Attention | Key/Value Heads | `num_kv_heads` | Integer | `0` | `0-4096` | The run | Key/value heads for grouped-query attention (LLaMA 2-70B/3, Mistral): fewer key/value heads than query heads shrink the generation cache and parameters. 0 = same as num_heads (standard); 1 = multi-query. Must divide num_heads. |
| Attention | Sliding Window | `sliding_window` | Integer | `0` | `0-1048576` | The run | Sliding-window attention (Mistral): each position sees at most this many most recent positions including itself. 0 = full causal attention. Useful only for contexts longer than the window. Advanced. |
| Attention | Attention Logit Soft-cap | `attn_logit_softcap` | Number | `0` | `0.0-1000.0` | The run | Attention logit soft-cap (Gemma 2): scores = cap \* tanh(scores / cap) keeps logits bounded. 0 = off; Gemma 2 uses 50. Advanced. |
| Block | Residual Init Scale | `residual_init_scale` | Number | `1.0` | `0.001-10.0` | The run | Multiplies the starting weights of the attention output and feed-forward down projections. GPT-2 uses 1/sqrt(2 x number of blocks) so deep stacks start stable (e.g. 0.354 for 4 blocks, 0.204 for 12). Affects initialization only. Advanced. |
| Fine-tuning | Frozen | `frozen` | On / off | `false` |   | The run | Keeps this layer's weights as they are while the rest of the model trains: no gradient step, no weight decay, no optimizer memory. Use it on layers that start from a weights file (fine-tuning), then turn it off to train them too. |

**Read by** says whether a run uses the setting (**The run**) or only the editor, a dialog or a view (**The editor only**).

## Usage

```text
Stack multiple nodes for depth. Internal attention projections and Dense/FC layers are owned by this composite node; edit dim_feedforward to change the hidden Dense width. Add another TransformerDecoder node to add a block. The Memory pin is reserved and fails closed when connected because cross-attention is not yet owned by the Studio runtime.
```

## Tips

- d_model must divide evenly by num_heads.
- Autoregressive generation loops remain a separate future contract.
- position_encoding=rope/alibi, qk_norm, grouped-query attention and soft-capping run on the ArrayFire attention path (the CPU is ArrayFire's CPU backend)
